content.title: Where to watch Spurs vs. Clippers NBA game free tonight during NBC and FuboTV dispute
content.text: The San Antonio Spurs hit the road for Los Angeles on Monday night and a Western Conference matchup with the Clippers. The game is scheduled to start at 10 p.m. ET (7 p.m. PT) with TV coverage on NBCSN Extra and streaming on-demand.NBCSN Extra is part of the NBC Universal family of networks currently blacked out on FuboTV during ongoing contract negotiations. Available streaming alternatives are listed below.How to watch Spurs vs. Clippers on TV and stream without cable:When:Monday, March 16 at 10 p.m. ET (7 p.m. PT)Where: Intuit Dome, Inglewood, Calif.TV channel: NBCSN Extra and PeacockStreaming on: DirecTV (free trial) | SlingTV (low intro rate) | Peacock ($10.99+/mo.)Spurs vs. Clippers: The matchupThe Spurs enter Monday’s contest as 9.5-point favorites and looking for their 50th win of the season. Last time out, San Antonio bounced back from a 136-131 loss to the Denver Nuggets with a home win over the Charlotte Hornets (115-102) on Saturday. Victor Wembanyama delivered 32 points, 12 rebounds, eight assists and four blocks in a massive effort to get the Spurs back in the win column for the 17th time in their past 19 games.See also: More NBA coverage on PennLiveThe Clippers got a double dose of bad news on Saturday with a 118-109 loss to the Sacramento Kings where star forward Kawhi Leonard exited late with a sprained ankle. The 34-year-old former Spur is listed as doubtful for Monday’s contest, which is fueling the early point spread in favor of the visiting Spurs. The Clips sit at 34-33 for the season after having a four-game winning streak snapped by the Kings, which is the eighth-best mark in the West.Spurs vs. Clippers: Know your live streamsDirecTV (free trial): DirecTV offers a 5-day free trial and a total of $30 off over the first three full months for the Choice Package, which includes 125-plus channels and access to ESPN Unlimited, a $29.99 standalone value featuring all ESPN channels and ESPN+.SlingTV (low intro rate): First full month of streaming runs as low as $29.99 with current offer for 50% off Sling’s Orange & Blue Plan. Day passes are also available for 24 hours ($4.99), as well as three-day ($9.99) and seven-day access ($14.99).Peacock ($10.99+/mo.): Peacock’s library of live sports is growing and features exclusive NFL and college football games, all in addition to NBC Universal movies, television series, and more.©2026 Advance Local Media LLC.
